_comment: Field NAMES both runtimes' flight recorders must agree on. Read by typescript/src/flight-recorder/key-redaction-parity.test.ts and python/tests/test_key_redaction_parity.py, so a name added to one list cannot silently miss the other. Its sibling value-redaction-corpus.json covers the other half of the question: that file asks whether a VALUE looks like a secret, this one asks whether a KEY says it is one. A value that looks like nothing in particular -- an opaque random string, which is what most API keys and session keys are -- can only be caught by its key.
_must_redact_comment: Every name here was written to the flight log in the clear before this corpus existed. The flight recorder carried its own copy of the secret-key rules that matched `token`, `secret` and `authorization` as exact words while matching `password`, `credential` and `cookie` as prefixes, so the singular was redacted and the plural was not.
_must_keep_comment: Redacting these would be a bug of the opposite kind. A ledger that blanks ordinary fields keeps the record and loses the ability to read it, and every one of these has been over-matched by some earlier version of these rules: `keyCount` and `monkey` were both blanked by a substring list that has since been narrowed.
